scope_note: Schema audit, not a run. No runtime exists; nothing is executed. The candidate schema is DESIGN-protocol-uptake section 3's ProtocolUptake record. The audited set is exactly the nine semantic INPUT fields the design names as candidates: six context_signal ids and three protocol_witness fields. Next-state projection fields (protocol_id, stack_after, pending_request_id, authority_delta) are outputs; they are outside this audit and are not B9 mutants — their necessity is the section 4 equivalence rule (B6) and the empty-authority_delta predicate (B3). Necessity arguments name transition rules only; fixtures do not exist yet and no argument below cites a fixture family. B9's mutants are later drawn at U-P0 from exactly the fields verdicted SURVIVES here.

audit.necessity: The probe_reply family's required signal predicate holds only when pending_need carries a live probe-type need's identity, and the resume rule binds a reply only to the request whose identity matches; change the value (absence sentinel, different identity, non-probe type) and the admission outcome changes from a selected probe_reply to refusal or a different selected move.

The quoted_datum family's required predicate is quote_boundary set, and the greeting family's required-absence predicate includes it; flipping the value flips which of those two admission rules can hold, changing the selected move or producing refusal.

The expected_output family's required predicate conjoins a set expected_output_slot, and greeting's required-absence predicate includes it; clearing the value removes the only rule that can admit an expected_output move, changing the outcome to refusal or another family.

The expected_output family's required predicate conjoins a live active_task with the slot, because an output slot can go stale after its task exits; with the slot set and active_task absent the conjunction fails and the admission outcome changes from a selected expected_output move to refusal.

audit.necessity_absent: No transition rule reads it. Family admission is decided by the four families' required signal-value predicates, none of which names prior_move; suspension and resumption are decided by protocol_stack, and reply binding by pending_need's identity. There is no rule whose outcome any value of prior_move changes, so under the U-PRE criterion the field is deleted, not retained as inert provenance.

audit.necessity: The stack rules read its value directly: the depth cap refuses a push when the stack already holds eight episodes, RESUME/EXIT legality depends on which episode is on top, and a reply for a suspended child may not bind in its parent; change the stack value and each of those outcomes changes.

The candidate set is built from witnessed protocol nodes and protocol_id is inside the four-field next-state projection; a different node id yields a different candidate protocol (or a dangling reference that fails validation), changing the selected move, the ASK partition by next_state_sha256, or the verdict.

The relation names which move family the sealed corpus witnesses the normalized surface under, and the admission predicate pairs exactly that family's required signal predicates with the position; a different relation value consults a different family's rule and the admission outcome changes.

audit.necessity_absent: Not a semantic input: no admission, stack, or binding rule's outcome changes with its value. B1's witness-to-builder resolution goes through protocol_node_id to the generated node and its single committed builder (scripts/build_protocol_corpus.py), so provenance survives the deletion. A surviving source_seed would owe a B9 mutant that cannot change any outcome, which B9 forbids.

consequences: U-P0's prereg records exactly the five surviving context_signal ids and two surviving protocol_witness fields; the ProtocolUptake schema is frozen without prior_move and without source_seed.
B9 seals exactly seven mutants, one per survivor, each naming its target fixture at U-P0.
No schema field may be removed after U-P0; this audit is the only pruning stage.
